title: One-step update of a work cell
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean work-tape symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $t\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\tau$ be a work-tape index, and let $p\in\mathbb{Z}$. After $t+1$ steps, the contents of cell $p$ on tape $\tau$ equal the symbol left in the cell by the step if $p$ is the tape head's position after $t$ steps; otherwise they equal the contents of that cell after $t$ steps. The symbol left by the step is the current scanned symbol if the machine is halted, and otherwise is the symbol prescribed by the transition (or the current scanned symbol if no write is prescribed).
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
replaced:
Let $M$ be a binary multi-tape Turing machine with finite state set $Q$, transition function
$\delta$ and $k$ work tapes whose cells are indexed by $\mathbb{Z}$; let $x \in \{0,1\}^*$,
$t \in \mathbb{N}$, $\tau \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$ and $p \in \mathbb{Z}$. Let $q \in Q \cup
\{\bot\}$ (with $\bot$ meaning halted), $a$ and $b = (b_0, \dots, b_{k-1})$ be the state, the
input-head symbol and the work-head symbols after $t$ steps of $M$ on $x$, and let $h$ be the
position of the head of work tape $\tau$ at that time. Then after $t + 1$ steps, cell $p$ of
work tape $\tau$ has the same content as after $t$ steps if $p \ne h$; if $p = h$, its
content is $b_\tau$ when $q = \bot$, and otherwise is the symbol that $\delta(q, a, b)$ writes
on tape $\tau$, or $b_\tau$ when that transition writes nothing on tape $\tau$.
